hints: Think of $K_{stab}$ in the same way as $K_c$, products over reactants with each concentration raised to its stoichiometric coefficient in the balanced equation for equilibrium I.
To find units, substitute $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ for every concentration term and cancel, remembering the $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ term is raised to the power 4.
walkthrough:
Write the equilibrium law for complex formation**
You have $\text{Cd}^{2+} + 4\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 \rightleftharpoons [\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4]^{2+}$. Just like any $K_c$, put the concentration of the complex ion on top and multiply the concentrations of the metal ion and ligand on the bottom. The 4 in front of $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ becomes a power 4: $$K_{stab} = \frac{[\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4^{2+}]}{[\text{Cd}^{2+}][\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2]^4}$$

Work out the units carefully**
Put $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ in for each bracket: $$\text{units} = \frac{\text{mol dm}^{-3}}{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^4} = \frac{1}{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^4}$$ Flip it to positive powers: $\text{mol}^{-4}\text{dm}^{12}$. A large positive power like this is normal when four ligands are involved.

hints: Start by finding the equilibrium concentrations of free $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ and the complex if the initial $1.00 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ is reduced by a factor of 1000.
Substitute those two values plus $K_{stab} = 3.6 \times 10^6$ into your expression from (a)(i) and rearrange to solve for $[\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2]$, noting it is a fourth root.
walkthrough:
Find what is left at equilibrium**
Initial $[\text{Cd}^{2+}] = 1.00 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$. Reduced by a factor of 1000 means divide by 1000: $$[\text{Cd}^{2+}]_{eqm} = 1.00 \times 10^{-7} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$ Almost all the cadmium has been converted to complex, so: $$[[\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4]^{2+}] \approx 1.00 \times 10^{-4} - 1.00 \times 10^{-7} = 9.99 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$

Substitute into Kstab and solve for ligand**
Let $y = [\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2]_{eqm}$: $$3.6 \times 10^6 = \frac{9.99 \times 10^{-5}}{(1.00 \times 10^{-7})y^4}$$ Rearrange: $$y^4 = \frac{9.99 \times 10^{-5}}{(1.00 \times 10^{-7})(3.6 \times 10^6)}$$ $$y = \sqrt[4]{0.2775} = 0.129 \approx 0.13 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$ That is the free amine concentration needed to drive the equilibrium that far to the right.

Final answer: At equilibrium: $[\text{Cd}^{2+}] = 1.00 \times 10^{-7} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$, $[[\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4]^{2+}] \approx 9.99 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$
$3.6 \times 10^6 = 9.99 \times 10^{-5} / (1.00 \times 10^{-7} \times [\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2]^4)$ giving $[\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2] = 0.13 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$

hints: Remember $\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq)$ is really $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, so both reactions involve breaking $\text{Cd-O}$ bonds to water and making new $\text{Cd-N}$ bonds to amine nitrogen atoms.
walkthrough:
See what enthalpy really measures here**
In water, $\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq)$ is $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$. To form either complex you must break $\text{Cd-O}$ bonds to water and make $\text{Cd-N}$ bonds to the amine nitrogen. In equilibrium I you make four $\text{Cd-N}$ bonds, in equilibrium II you also make four $\text{Cd-N}$ bonds from two bidentate $en$ ligands. Because the same type of bond is broken and the same type of bond is formed in both cases, the overall heat change is almost identical.

Final answer: Both equilibria involve formation of $\text{Cd-N}$ bonds and breaking of $\text{Cd-O}$ bonds, with the same number and similar types of bonds made and broken, so $\Delta H^\circ$ values are very similar.

hints: Use $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$ rearranged to $\Delta S^\circ = (\Delta H^\circ - \Delta G^\circ)/T$ with $T = 298 \text{ K}$ and convert kJ to J.
walkthrough:
Apply the Gibbs equation**
You know $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$, so flip it: $$\Delta S^\circ = \frac{\Delta H^\circ - \Delta G^\circ}{T}$$ For equilibrium II: $$\Delta S^\circ = \frac{(-56.5 - (-60.7)) \times 1000}{298} = \frac{+4.2 \times 1000}{298} = +14.1 \text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$$ Watch the units. $\Delta H$ and $\Delta G$ are in kJ, so multiply by 1000 to get J for entropy.

hints: Compare the total number of solute particles on each side and recall that one bidentate 1,2-diaminoethane molecule replaces two water molecules, while one methylamine replaces only one.
walkthrough:
Count particles to judge disorder**
Entropy increases when you create more independent particles. Each $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ is monodentate and frees only one $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Each $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ ($en$) is bidentate and frees two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules. So equilibrium II produces more free water molecules per ligand and has a smaller decrease in total solute moles. That is the chelate effect. Hence $\Delta S^\circ$ for II ($+14.1$) is much more positive than for I ($-66.8$).

Final answer: Equilibrium II has a more positive $\Delta S^\circ$ because fewer moles of solute combine to form the complex, one $en$ displaces two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ whereas one $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ displaces only one $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so there is less loss of disorder.

hints: Recall that a larger $K_{stab}$ and a more negative $\Delta G^\circ$ both mean the equilibrium lies further to the right and the complex is more stable, then compare the given values for I and II.
walkthrough:
Link data to stability**
A more stable complex means formation is more favoured. Look at the numbers: $K_{stab}$ for II is $4.2 \times 10^{10}$, about ten thousand times larger than for I. Equally, $\Delta G^\circ$ for II is $-60.7 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, much more negative than $-37.4 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for I. Both point the same way, so the bidentate $en$ complex $[\text{Cd}(en)_2]^{2+}$ is the more stable one, driven by the favourable entropy you just calculated.

Final answer: $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2)_2]^{2+}$ from equilibrium II is more stable because $K_{stab}$ is larger ($4.2 \times 10^{10}$ vs $3.6 \times 10^6$) / $\Delta G^\circ$ is more negative ($-60.7$ vs $-37.4 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).
